headline: A relief rally after the October AI selloff: demand signals are strong, but the money is moving from leveraged builders to whoever owns power and memory.
regime: AI-bottleneck stocks bounced on Oct 21 (semis ETF +2.0%, servers +4.2%) after SpaceX's earnings and Super Micro's preliminary beat, but the month is still deeply red: semis -6.5%, memory -17%, neoclouds -26%. With the 10-year yield above 5.1% and crude near $97, the market is paying for cash flow and punishing debt-funded capacity. Software was the only segment up over the month.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Musk calls power, cooling and electrical equipment the limiting factor for AI (2f7c642d23d0)
Analysts project 194 GW of hyperscaler demand by 2035 against a grid that is not ready (72e5a06e0019)
NextDC's 40% drop came from power constraints and local opposition slowing its build (81d7dcc8478c)
Venture Global's GE Vernova deal could unlock up to 10 GW for data centres (603f95f12f4e)
theses.change_note: First worldview. The strongest and most repeated theme in today's news.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Google Cloud is turning away customers for lack of AI capacity (7376ff0b73c3)
Super Micro's preliminary quarter came in far above guidance on AI platform demand (4141a906919e)
SpaceX says its AI chips pay for themselves in under a year (a5c4a0c75798)
Anthropic has committed over $600B to compute and wants more (63abd5d5150d)
theses.change_note: First worldview. The October selloff was about financing and valuation, not a demand miss.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave debt fell again after a Korean neocloud IPO flopped (f981148c26f6)
Michael Burry is short Nebius (a5c4a0c75798)
CoreWeave and NuScale hit 52-week lows while other AI names recovered (31401af0fb90)
The neocloud segment is down 26% in a month, the worst of any segment
theses.change_note: First worldview. Matches this week's TradingAgents calls: IREN Sell, NBIS Underweight.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Micron trades near 5x earnings with 81-87% margins (3e89bedcd3a2)
Micron has contracts stretching toward 2030 yet fell hard last week (4db3a1b67d58)
Memory names are down 17% in a month despite revenue growth above 300% at Micron and SanDisk
theses.change_note: First worldview. Confidence held to 55 because a 5x P/E on peak margins is the classic cyclical trap.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Meta's free cash flow fell 91% as data-centre costs climb (57ca0d6a99f5)
Amazon plans $200B of capex with deeply negative free cash flow (4a273cb1dec4)
Alphabet is down about $860B from its peak while Apple, which avoided the race, is near highs (2178e0d1afb7)
theses.change_note: First worldview. Good for suppliers, bad for the spenders' own returns.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: NVIDIA and Micron alone are 36% of S&P 500 earnings growth (4d4eb482ab87)
Ken Griffin calls AI 'almost certainly' a bubble (6b4b1290b7a3)
Berkshire hit a record as investors rotated out of chips, a dot-com-era signal (15143826f116)
The US 10-year yield is 5.11%
theses.change_note: First worldview. The main reason to size AI exposure as a slice, not the whole portfolio.

compute.note: Demand is real but these are the most crowded names; -11% in a month.

foundry_equipment.note: Moody's upgraded TSMC; equipment names still down 10% in a month.

memory_storage.note: Cheapest earnings in the universe after a 17% monthly drop; cyclical risk is the catch.

networking_optical.note: Growth is strong (Credo, Arista) but the segment fell 13% in a month.

servers.note: Super Micro's beat lifted the group; thin margins limit the upside.

power_nuclear.note: The bottleneck thesis; prefer generators with cash flow over pre-revenue nuclear.

grid_electrical.note: Transformers and grid equipment are the slowest part of the build to expand.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv earnings next week will test this.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Credit stress, dilution and no-customer projects; avoid until financing clears.

hyperscalers.note: Capacity-constrained growth, but capex is crushing free cash flow.

ai_software.note: Only segment up over the month; momentum, not value.

risks: A 10-year yield above 5% compresses valuations across the whole AI chain.
Memory earnings at 5x may be peak-cycle; a pricing turn would cut them fast.
Credit stress at neoclouds could spread to their suppliers through cancelled orders.
Market concentration: two chip names carry over a third of S&P earnings growth.
watch: Meta and Tesla earnings after the close: capex guidance and data-centre spend.
Vertiv earnings next week as a read on cooling demand.
CoreWeave bond prices as the stress gauge for leveraged AI capacity.
Whether the Oct 21 bounce holds in semis or fades like the neocloud names.
